b: An easy 3,000er by Dolomites standards, from the Sass Pordoi cable car.

pk.x: At the pass, by the Sass Pordoi cable car.

d.n: Wide balcony path.

b: Old smugglers' path facing the Marmolada glacier.

pk.x: At the pass.

d.n: Flat lakeshore.

b: Lake with the Sorapiss and Tre Cime around it; good for an evening walk.

pk.x: Charged 08:00–20:00 in season; free in winter.

d.n: Adamello-Brenta Nature Park: leash.

b: The lake that used to turn red, in the Brenta Dolomites.

pk.x: Book online (PNAB) by 06:00 on the day, daily mid-June to late September and autumn weekends.

d.n: Hot and shadeless in summer; shared with bikes.

b: Old cliff road carved above Lake Garda, now for walkers and bikes.

d.n: Check muzzle rules for the rotating cable car.

lf: Rotating cable car from Malcesine.
b: Ridge path 2,000 m above Lake Garda.

pk.x: 170 underground spaces at the cable car; open 08:00–19:30.

n: Sentiero del Viandante: Varenna to Bellano

d.n: Mule tracks; train back to Varenna.

lf: Train back along the lake.
b: Old mule path above Lake Como, past Vezio castle.

d.n: Level path along an old irrigation channel.

b: Level path beside an old irrigation channel through vineyards above Merano.

d.n: Wide, almost level balcony path; inns at Gerstreit and Söldenköpfl.

lf: Bus 845 (RVO) stops at the Zipfhäusl. Söldenköpfl inn is closed on Fridays.
b: A level walk along the old brine pipeline high above the Ramsau valley, with the Watzmann and Hochkalter opposite the whole way.

d.n: Steep, stony zigzags below the Steinerne Rinne; the hut takes dogs only by prior arrangement with the hosts.

lf: Toll road through the Kaiserbachtal from Griesenau to the Griesner Alm car park; in summer a free hiking bus runs to the valley car park.
b: Short, steep climb to the pass between the Wilder and Zahmer Kaiser, right under the walls of the Totenkirchl and Fleischbank. The Stripsenkopf viewpoint is 1¾ h further.

pk.f: Parking free; toll road €6 per car
pk.x: Pay at the toll machine. Road closed roughly mid-January to end of February.
At the foot of the toll road in Griesenau, 5 km below; hiking bus in summer.

d.n: Mostly forest roads; young cattle on the alm pastures; the lake for a drink on the way back.

lf: Paid car park at the Seestüberl. Walleralm, Stöfflhütte and Kafma Alm on top; check opening days.
b: Up through the forest to a cluster of alm huts on a sunny meadow below the Scheffauer, back along the quiet south shore of the Hintersteiner See.

pk.x: At the east end of the lake.

d.n: Lech riverbank, gravel lanes and fields; the small lake and the Lech for a drink.

lf: Park at the parish church in Lechaschau (bus stop Lechaschau Gemeindeamt).
b: Along the Lech and up past little chapels to a small bathing lake with the Frauenseestube inn, then back across the open fields of Lechaschau.

pk.x: By the parish church; bus stop Lechaschau Gemeindeamt.

d.n: Steep rocky path with a short wire-rope passage below the hut; walk round the Roßstein on the north side to avoid it. Leave the Buchstein scramble out.

lf: Paid car park Bayerwald on the B307 south of Kreuth. The hut's goods lift failed in September 2026: limited menu, and the 2027 season depends on its repair.
b: The 'eagle's nest' hut wedged between two limestone towers, with the Roßstein summit a few minutes away and the Buchstein (grade II) for the sure-footed.

pk.x: On the B307 south of Kreuth.

d.n: High open terrain on the Schmugglersteig; little shade. Check the dog rules on the Komperdell and Lazid lifts.

lf: Dorfbahn, Komperdellbahn and Lazidbahn up from Serfaus (free car park at the village entrance); watch the last lift down. Hut open July to September.
b: High-level path on the old smugglers' route with information boards, to the little Hexenseen lakes and the Cologne section's hut at 2,588 m near the Swiss border.

pk.x: At the village entrance; the village metro and lifts take you up.

n: Wilder Kaiser crossing: Ellmauer Tor & Steinerne Rinne

d.n: Cable-secured, exposed ledges on the Eggersteig and loose rock in the Steinerne Rinne: not for dogs.

lf: One way: leave a car at each end or take a taxi back (Griesner Alm is up the Kaiserbachtal toll road from Griesenau). Helmet; a via ferrata set is recommended. Snow often lies in the Steinerne Rinne until July.
b: The classic crossing through the heart of the Wilder Kaiser: up the Kübelkar to the Ellmauer Tor, then down the walled gully of the Steinerne Rinne under the Fleischbank and Predigtstuhl to the Stripsenjoch.

pk.x: Very large terraced car park at the trailhead. Free hiking bus from Ellmau with the Wilder Kaiser guest card.

pk.f: Parking free; toll road €6 per car
pk.x: Pay at the toll machine. Road closed roughly mid-January to end of February.

d.n: Iron rungs, a ladder and cable-secured climbing (via ferrata B): not for dogs. The Gruttenhütte is a fine place to wait.

lf: Helmet essential (rockfall from parties above); harness and via ferrata set recommended. Queues on the Jägerwand rungs on summer weekends. Gruttenhütte open early June to mid-October.
b: The highest summit of the Kaisergebirge by its normal route: past the Gruttenhütte, up the Hochgrubach cirque and the 74 rungs of the Jägerwand to the little Babenstuber shelter just below the top.

pk.x: Very large terraced car park at the trailhead. Free hiking bus from Ellmau with the Wilder Kaiser guest card.

d.n: A secured chimney and several cabled passages above the hut: not for dogs.

lf: Signposted 3¼ h from the Wochenbrunner Alm. Dry weather only; the notch can also be crossed north to the Stripsenjochhaus.
b: From the Gruttenhütte terrace up a grassy rib and a secured chimney, past the Kaindl-Stewart tower, to the notch between the Ellmauer Halt and the Karlspitzen.

pk.x: Very large terraced car park at the trailhead. Free hiking bus from Ellmau with the Wilder Kaiser guest card.

n: Gruttenhütte round from Ellmau via the Riedlhütte

d.n: Steep and partly rocky on path 825 down from the Gruttenhütte; streams in the Spatlahner gorge on the way back.

lf: Starts at the hiking start point by the Ellmau tourist office. Riedlhütte open May to October; check the huts' opening days.
b: A full day from the village: across the Biedringer meadows to the little Riedlhütte, steeply up to the Gruttenhütte, the highest hut on the Wilder Kaiser, and down past the Wochenbrunner Alm and through the Spatlahner gorge.

pk.x: Public car park in the village centre, near the tourist office.

n: Spatlahner gorge to the Wochenbrunner Alm

d.n: Stream all the way up; leash by the deer and ibex enclosure at the Alm.

lf: In summer a free hiking bus runs between Ellmau and the Wochenbrunner Alm, so you can walk one way. Add 20 min for the Stations of the Cross path to the St. Anna grotto above the Alm.
b: Up from Ellmau along the Hausbach and through the little Spatlahner gorge to the Wochenbrunner Alm, with its game enclosure and terrace under the Kaiser walls, and the forest path to the St. Anna grotto.

pk.x: Public car park in the village centre, near the tourist office.

d.n: Forest and meadow paths; short steep sections near the top.

lf: Signposted from the Wochenbrunner Alm via the Bergsteigergrab memorial (1½ h to the top).
b: A small grassy top on the south side of the Kaiser with a big view of the Kitzbühel Alps, past the climbers' memorial, then down to the Gaudeamushütte for lunch.

pk.x: Very large terraced car park at the trailhead. Free hiking bus from Ellmau with the Wilder Kaiser guest card.

d.n: A short cable-and-footrest climbing spot before the Hoher Brand and a 2 m rock step below the top: not suitable for dogs.

lf: Griesen station is on the Außerfern railway, about every two hours from Garmisch; hikers' car park at the west end of the village. No huts on the way. Go up and down via the Schellalm: the Sunkensattel descent has become loose and slippery.
b: A quiet, steep summit on the border ridge of the Ammergau Alps, via the Schellalm and the Brandjoch ridge, looking straight across the Loisach at the Zugspitze.

pk.x: West end of Griesen, just before the bridge (navigation address Griesen 7). Griesen station is 5 min away.

n: Friederspitz from the Ochsenhütte car park

d.n: Long: forest road, then grassy zigzags past the Friederalm; fine for a fit dog, little shade higher up.

lf: Car park on the Garmisch–Griesen road, about 5 km past Garmisch after the second level crossing; also signposted from Griesen (4¾ h). The twin summit, the Frieder (2050 m), is 30 min further.
b: Long, lonely climb past the Rotmoos and Friederalm pastures to a grassy double summit facing the whole Wetterstein, from the Zugspitze to the Alpspitze.

pk.x: On the Garmisch–Griesen road, about 5 km past Garmisch after the second level crossing.
Also signposted from Griesen (4¾ h).

d.n: Leash in the narrow, wet and busy gorge; after that the Partnach is beside you all day.

lf: Partnachklamm entry fee; if the gorge is closed, go round via the Partnachalm. Very long as a day: most people sleep at the hut (late May to mid-October) and return the next day.
b: The long walk up the wild Reintal: through the Partnach gorge, past the Bockhütte and the turquoise Blaue Gumpe pools, to the hut with the prayer flags where the Partnach rises.

pk.x: About 300 spaces; 25 min walk to the Partnachklamm. Fills quickly at weekends.

n: Schachen through the Reintal and Oberreintal

d.n: Leash in the gorge; the climb into the Oberreintal is 55 steep zigzags and a scree crossing. Dogs may not stay at the Oberreintalhütte.

lf: Partnachklamm entry fee. Signposted 5 h from the Partnach (Bockhütte 2¼ h, Oberreintal 4 h). Return the same way or down the Kälbersteig; the Schachenhaus makes it a two-day trip.
b: The wild way to King Ludwig's mountain house: up the Reintal, then steeply into the hidden Oberreintal cirque under the climbers' walls, and over to the Schachen and its alpine garden.

pk.x: About 300 spaces; 25 min walk to the Partnachklamm. Fills quickly at weekends.

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Forest path, easy for paws.

lf: Starts at the big Königssee car park. The Rabenwand viewpoint is a short detour from the top of the loop; don't follow the old overgrown shore path beyond the Malerwinkel.
b: The classic first look down the Königssee towards St. Bartholomä and the Watzmann, on an easy forest loop from the car park.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €7 for 3 h, €9 per day
pk.x: About 1,800 spaces, 5 min to the boats and the Jennerbahn; EV charging.

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Wet wooden stairs and walkways in the gorge.

lf: Small entry fee for the gorge (ticket machine). The gorge alone is a 20-minute walk from the Wimbachbrücke car park; not for prams.
b: Through the short, spray-filled Wimbach gorge and up the quiet valley to the old royal hunting lodge, now an inn, under the Watzmann and Hochkalter.

pk.f: €6 up to 4 h, €9 for the day
pk.x: About 200 spaces; coins (no change) or Parkster. Bus 846 stops here.

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Cattle on the Kühroint and Schapbach pastures.

lf: Hikers' car park Hammerstiel above Schönau. The Grünstein summit is a short detour on the way up.
b: Over the Grünstein to the alm meadows of Kühroint under the Watzmann, then to the Archenkanzel, a balcony 750 m straight above the Königssee and St. Bartholomä.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €5 for 3 h, €6 per day
pk.x: No sleeping in vehicles; accessible WC.

pk.f: €6 up to 4 h, €9 for the day
pk.x: About 200 spaces; coins (no change) or Parkster. Bus 846 stops here.

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Muzzle on the Königssee boats.

lf: Königssee boat to St. Bartholomä (summer timetable). The ice cave has collapsed: don't go into it or onto the snowfield. Streams can be high in early summer.
b: From the red-domed pilgrimage church across the lake to the lowest permanent snowfield in the German Alps, right at the foot of the 1,800 m Watzmann east face.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €7 for 3 h, €9 per day
pk.x: About 1,800 spaces, 5 min to the boats and the Jennerbahn; EV charging.

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. The Antonigraben descent is steep; the way via Fernseben is gentler.

lf: Starts at the national park info point Klausbachhaus. Descend by the steep Antonigraben straight to the Hintersee, or the easier way via Fernseben, then along the shore.
b: Up broad zigzags to a little alm with a bench and cross looking straight down on the Hintersee, then back along the lake.

pk.x: At the national park info point on the Hirschbichlstraße.

n: Ramsau to the Hintersee through the Zauberwald

d.n: Along the Ramsauer Ache all the way; leash on the busy lake path.

lf: Starts at the Neuhausenbrücke by Ramsau church. Return the same way through the Zauberwald, or via the Wartstein and the Kunterweg pilgrimage church (about 1 h more).
b: From the famous Ramsau church up the Ramsauer Ache past the glacier mills and the Marxenklamm, through the mossy boulders of the Zauberwald and once round the Hintersee.

pk.x: Ramsau village, Im Tal.

n: Jenner from Hinterbrand via the Wasserfallalm

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Rocky final steps to the top; dogs ride the Jennerbahn.

lf: Hinterbrand car park above Schönau. Down by the Jennerbahn (or on foot the same way). Huts: Mittelstation, Wasserfallalm, Mitterkaseralm, Jenneralm.
b: The shorter way up the Jenner, past three alms and up the old ski run to the summit balcony over the Königssee and the Watzmann east face.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €5 for 3 h, €6 per day
pk.x: Scharitzkehlstraße; no overnight stays.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €7 for 3 h, €9 per day
pk.x: About 1,800 spaces, 5 min to the boats and the Jennerbahn; EV charging.

n: Jenner to the Mittelstation via the Schneibsteinhaus

d.n: Berchtesgaden National Park: dogs on a leash. Mostly downhill; cattle on the Königsberg and Königsbach alms.

lf: Jennerbahn up to the top station, back down from the middle station. The Jenner summit is 20 min from the top station.
b: A mostly downhill walk from the top of the Jennerbahn to the Schneibsteinhaus on the edge of the high karst plateau, then down past the Königsbergalm and Königsbachalm on the Königsweg.

pk.f: €3 per hour, €7 for 3 h, €9 per day
pk.x: About 1,800 spaces, 5 min to the boats and the Jennerbahn; EV charging.

d.n: Karwendel nature park: leash. Rocky path down from the Hafelekar; muzzle in the cable cars.

lf: Nordkettenbahnen from Innsbruck to the Hafelekar; walk down to the Seegrube station and ride from there.
b: Ten minutes from the top station to Innsbruck's summit cross, looking down 1,700 m onto the city and north into the Karwendel, then down the rocky slope to the Seegrube terrace.

pk.x: At the Seegrubenbahn valley station (Nordkettenbahnen); or park in town and take the Hungerburgbahn from the Congress.

n: Höttinger Bild & Rauschbrunnen from the Planötzenhof

d.n: Forest roads and paths above Innsbruck.

lf: Free car park at the Planötzenhof above Hötting. The Rauschbrunnen inn is closed on Mondays.
b: A short forest walk above Innsbruck to the little pilgrimage chapel of the Höttinger Bild and on to the Rauschbrunnen inn, with its terrace over the Inn valley.

pk.x: Above Hötting, Innsbruck.

d.n: Karwendel nature park: leash. Narrow, exposed gorge path with cable handholds.

lf: Starts at the Karwendel nature park info centre in Scharnitz (paid parking). Can be lengthened to the Möslalm (15 km).
b: Along the young Isar and into the narrow Gleirsch gorge, its path cut into the rock above turquoise pools, back over the Gleirschhöhe.

pk.x: At the Karwendel nature park info centre.
At the end of the Hinterautalstraße near the Isarlodge Wiesenhof; 10 km loop from here.

n: Bärenkopf via the Bärenbadalm and Weißenbachsattel

d.n: Karwendel nature park: leash. A short cable-secured rock step just below the top; dogs usually manage it.

lf: Paid car park by the Gasthof St. Hubertus before Pertisau. The Karwendel-Bergbahn from Pertisau halves the climb.
b: Up through the forest to the Bärenbadalm and the grassy top high above the Achensee, then round over the Weißenbachsattel.

pk.x: By the Gasthof St. Hubertus just before Pertisau.
At the valley station in Pertisau; the fee is refunded with a lift ticket.

n: Stuiben falls, Frauenbrünnele & Kleiner Plansee from Reutte

d.n: Lake shore and streams all the way; steps on the Hermannsteig by the falls.

lf: Starts by the power station on the Archbach, just off the Fernpass road at Reutte.
b: Up the Ministersteig to the quiet Kleiner Plansee, past the little Frauenbrünnele chapel, and down the Hermannsteig beside the Stuiben waterfalls.

pk.x: By the power station on the Archbach, just off the Fernpass road.

n: Rigi Panorama Trail: Kaltbad to Scheidegg

d.n: Wide, level path on the old railway line; cattle on the pastures.

lf: Up by rack railway from Vitznau or cable car from Weggis; down by the Rigi Scheidegg cable car to Kräbel and the train from Goldau.
b: Level walk on the bed of an old mountain railway, through tunnels and along balconies above Lake Lucerne, from Rigi Kaltbad to the quieter Rigi Scheidegg.

pk.x: Rack railway to Rigi Kaltbad and Kulm.
Cable car to Rigi Kaltbad.

d.n: Several stream crossings and a few cable-protected bits above the Gaisalpe.

lf: Small car park in Reichenbach near Oberstdorf; arrive early. Berggasthof Gaisalpe on the way.
b: Past the Gaisalpe inn and its waterfall to a clear cirque lake under the Rubihorn, warm enough for a swim in high summer.

pk.x: Small car park south of the St. Jakobus chapel in Reichenbach (815 m); arrive early.

n: Rubihorn from Reichenbach via the Gaisalpsee

d.n: Steep and exposed in places above the lake, with cable protection: only for a sure-footed dog.

lf: Can be made a loop over the Gaisalphorn and down the Wallrafweg (about 15 km, 1,300 m).
b: Oberstdorf's steep pyramid, past the Gaisalpe and the Gaisalpsee to a summit looking over the whole Oberstdorf valley and the Allgäu main ridge.

pk.x: Small car park south of the St. Jakobus chapel in Reichenbach (815 m); arrive early.

n: Oytal to the Oytalhaus on the Dr.-Hohenadel-Weg

d.n: Along the Oybach most of the way.

lf: From the Nebelhornbahn car park in Oberstdorf, up the Oytal road and back on the Dr.-Hohenadel-Weg along the stream. The Stuibenfall is about 45 min beyond the Oytalhaus.
b: Gentle valley walk from Oberstdorf into the Oytal under the steep grass flanks of the Höfats, to the Oytalhaus inn.

pk.x: At the Nebelhorn cable car valley station in Oberstdorf.

d.n: Forest road and path; cattle on the Ehrwalder Alm and Seebenalm.

lf: Ehrwalder Almbahn up from Ehrwald. Return the same way or by the forest road; the Coburger Hütte is 1 h above the lake.
b: The easy way to the Seebensee: from the top of the Almbahn through the Seebenwald past Ganghofers Rast to the lake that mirrors the Zugspitze.

pk.x: Valley station of the Ehrwalder Almbahn (Dr.-Ludwig-Ganghofer-Straße 66).

n: Kramerspitz loop via St. Martin and the Stepbergalm

d.n: Steep, rocky ridge with a few short wire-rope passages; with a dog, come down from the Stepbergalm by the easier Kreuzweg rather than the Gelbe Gwänd. No reliable water above St. Martin.

lf: St. Martinshütte is open most of the year (closed Tuesdays and in late November); the Stepbergalm runs May to October, closed Mondays. North-side snowfields linger into June.
b: The full round on Garmisch's home peak: up past St. Martin and the Felsenkanzel to the summit ridge facing the Zugspitze, down over the Predigtstuhl to the Stepbergalm and back along the Kramerplateauweg.

pk.x: In front of the Berggasthof Almhütte; full early on weekends.
Kramerhänge, for starting up the Kramerhänge to St. Martin.

n: Zugspitzplatt to the Ehrwalder Alm over the Gatterl

d.n: Rough scree on the Plattsteig and a short, exposed cable-secured rock step at the Gatterl where a dog must be led closely or helped. Cattle on the Ehrwalder Alm; streams below the Hochfeldernalm.

lf: Up by the Tiroler Zugspitzbahn and the Gletscherbahn down to Sonnalpin (or the Zahnradbahn from Garmisch), back down by the Ehrwalder Almbahn. Knorrhütte is open June to early October.
b: The stage from the Knorrhütte to Ehrwald as a day walk: down across the stony Zugspitzplatt to the hut, over the Gatterl into Austria and past the Feldernjöchl and the Hochfeldernalm to the Ehrwalder Alm.

pk.x: Valley station of the Tiroler Zugspitzbahn in Obermoos; the Ehrwalder Almbahn is 3 km away by bus or on foot.
Where the walk ends, at the Almbahn valley station.
